title: Redwood cost-econ discovery with Stratagem Capital
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private; customer has strong budget constraints (~$60k/mo) and emphasized latency SLOs for trading signals. Discussed batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, and scope for a pilot benchmark. Agreed next steps: send unit-cost model, share benchmark instructions, and schedule a pilot kickoff.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 00:52:00
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Ross (Head of ML, Stratagem), Daniel Kim (Infra), Priya Shah (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, uh thanks for carving out time. i'm maya from redwood, and with me is arjun our se. quick around the room?
[00:08] Olivia: hi i'm olivia, head of ml at stratagem. we run a few high-frequency signals apps, so cost per inference and latency are like, top of mind.
[00:15] Priya: priya here, cto. budget guidance - we have about 60k a month for model infra expansion this quarter.
[00:23] Daniel: daniel, infra eng. we'll own networking/VPC for anything private.
[00:27] Arjun: great, thanks. today we wanted to focus specifically on unit economics - per-token pricing, how batching and kv/prefix caching affect unit cost, and options between hosted, dedicated, and private. sound good?
[00:36] Olivia: yep, that sounds perfect.
[00:38] -- Summary / goal --
[00:40] Maya: our goal is to give you a ballpark on expected cost per 1k tokens across the different deployment modes and to outline levers you can pull to hit the 60k budget while meeting latency SLOs.

[00:52] Arjun: quick context questions - typical prompt and response lengths? qps and burst patterns?
[00:56] Olivia: most prompts are short, 30-80 tokens, responses usually 60-150 tokens. baseline qps is 20 per second, spikes to 80 for short windows.
[01:06] Daniel: retention/kv cache expectation: can we reuse prefix/context across many requests? yes, we do keep conversation state but also a lot of shared template prompts.
[01:14] Arjun: perfect, that means batching and prefix caching should help a lot.

[01:20] Maya: high-level pricing - hosted is straightforward per-token, dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token after reserved commit, private has more fixed platform fees but you control infra (and networking costs). i can walk numbers with a simple model.
[01:32] Olivia: want to understand the tipping points - at what QPS or token volume does dedicated become cheaper than hosted?
[01:38] Arjun: it depends on reservation level and concurrency. ballpark: if you're above ~30-140k tokens per minute consistently, dedicated reservation starts to make economic sense vs hosted. but caching changes that a lot; if you hit high kv cache reuse, effective token count drops.
[01:52] Priya: can you quantify caching? like how much can we expect to reduce billable tokens?
[01:56] Arjun: typical workloads with good prefix reuse see 20-60% reduction in billable tokens depending on hit rate. so if you have many shared template prompts or repeated prefixes, kv caching reduces both latency and token spend.
[02:09] Olivia: is that kv cache the same as redis or internal to your runtime? how does that work with private deploy?
[02:14] Arjun: it's runtime-managed KV cache for model kv states (not user key-value store). for hosted/dedicated it's native; for private/VPC we can integrate with customer-managed redis or you can use our runtime's local cache depending on constraints. with VPC there are extra network hop latencies to consider.
[02:29] Daniel: noted - network hops could be problematic for our sub-200ms SLO.

[02:33] Maya: let's talk per-token numbers - i want to be clear these are illustrative: hosted text-gen ~ $0.0035 per 1k tokens for our mid-size Llama family variants, embeddings separate. dedicated reserved economics can drop unit cost 30-50% at commit levels. private has a license/platform fee + infra, so break-even varies by month volume.
[02:52] Olivia: ok, so for our volume - 20 qps baseline, avg 100 tokens per call, that's about 120k tokens per minute? (brief pause) sorry math - hang on.
[03:03] Daniel: 20 qps * 100 tokens * 60 = 120k tokens/min, yes.
[03:10] Arjun: so monthly estimate ~ 120k*60*24*30 => 120k tokens/min * 60 = 7.2M tokens/hour * 24 * 30 ≈ 5.18B tokens/month baseline (this seems large) - but with caching and short prompts effective billed tokens could be much lower.
[03:33] Priya: that baseline would blow budget at hosted rates, so caching and batching are mandatory.
[03:38] Olivia: also we can tolerate slightly higher latency on non-critical models, but some models need <200ms p95.

[03:45] Arjun: batching helps with throughput, reduces GPU overhead, and the runtime's continuous batching can fold many small requests. however batching increases tail latency slightly; we tune maximal batch window and target latency SLOs. you can get good batching gains with window sizes ~10-25ms for low-latency apps.
[03:59] Daniel: so is there a recommended batch size for our qps?
[04:02] Arjun: with 20 qps baseline a small per-request batch window of 15-25ms should already group several requests; for spikes we'd autoscale. dedicated gives you more predictable concurrency so you can hit better batch sizes consistently.

[04:15] Maya: quantization - 4-bit quantization gives large memory and throughput improvements and reduces unit costs, but might impact some quality for certain prompt types. we recommend testing quantized variants in the evals. that can reduce cost per token further by 15-30% depending on model.
[04:31] Olivia: quality impact - acceptable for our scoring models maybe, but for final output we'll want to keep hallucination low. so we'll probably mix quantized lower-cost models for internal scoring and a higher-precision for final decisions.
[04:43] Arjun: that's a common pattern - routing policies can send high-confidence or production prompts to higher-precision model, cheaper ones to quantized. smart routing saves cost while preserving quality.

[04:53] Priya: security questions - SOC 2, SSO, KMS?
[04:56] Maya: yes we have SOC 2 in hosted and enterprise controls for dedicated/private. SSO / SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration are available for Dedicated and Private. we'll share the security pack.
[05:05] Daniel: if we do private on our VPC, are you able to support air-gapped?
[05:09] Maya: we offer on-prem packaging for regulated customers; leads to longer procurement but possible.

[05:15] Olivia: back to money - how would you structure a pilot to prove we can hit < $60k/mo effective spend?
[05:20] Arjun: pilot idea: 3-week benchmark. you supply a 2-week sample of prompts and traffic profile. we run hosted and a dedicated micro-reservation sim with quantized and non-quantized variants. we report billable token delta, p95 latency, and cost per 1k effective tokens.
[05:35] Maya: we'll also produce a simple unit-cost model (spreadsheet) showing break-evens for reservation sizes.
[05:40] Olivia: sounds good, we want the spreadsheet so we can model mixes (e.g., 70% quantized routing).

[05:47] Daniel: procurement timeline? we might need an NDA, security review in parallel.
[05:51] Maya: yes we can send NDA and security docs. procurement typical for dedicated/private is 4-8 weeks, hosted can be quicker.

[05:58] Priya: any obvious hidden costs we should watch for? network egress? monitoring data?
[06:02] Maya: good call - network egress for private can be material; observability retention, audit logs, and custom retention policies can add cost. we'll highlight these in the pricing sheet.

[06:12] Olivia: ok wrap up - big ask is: send the pricing model, runbook, security pack, and propose pilot dates.
[06:18] Maya: yep we'll do that. arjun will send the runbook.
[06:21] Arjun: i'll include example k8s config for our dedicated agent and the micro-benchmark harness.
[06:26] Maya: thanks everyone.
[06:28] Olivia: thanks, appreciate it.

-- End transcript (audio had occasional garble and mis-attributed words; names sometimes clipped)

Recap / Next steps:
- Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet and unit-cost model by 2026-03-23 (Maya)
- Redwood SE to share benchmark runbook + repo instructions by 2026-03-25 (Arjun)
- Stratagem to provide sample prompts and traffic profile by 2026-03-24 (Olivia)
- Schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-30
